stem: A 16-year-old girl living with HIV, on antiretroviral therapy followed at a local clinic, was identified for TB symptom screening during a routine outreach visit that systematically checks people living with HIV for TB, part of a standing program activity; she had not sought care specifically for her symptoms. She reports about six weeks of cough and worsening fatigue, which she and her family attributed to her usual HIV-related tiredness. Her most recent CD4 count, checked a month ago, was 85 cells/uL. No known TB contact in the household. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. Chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates with early cavitation. Exam: thin, oxygen saturation 95% on room air, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 37.8C, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.social_history: Lives with family in a rural household; living with HIV, on ART, followed at a local clinic
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and worsening fatigue, attributed initially to usual HIV-related tiredness
patient.exam_findings: Thin, SpO2 95% room air, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 37.8C, no lymphadenopathy, bilateral infiltrates with early cavitation on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; on established antiretroviral therapy; no prior TB treatment

distractors: Fatigue attributed to her usual HIV-related tiredness rather than a new, superimposed infectious process
Low CD4 count treated as a chronic baseline finding rather than prompting focused TB screening given her known risk
Mild fever attributed to a minor, self-limited viral illness rather than investigated further
ntep_correct_actions: Recognize that this patient's case was appropriately identified through routine active case-finding targeted at people living with HIV, consistent with standing national program policy rather than a threshold-gated activity.
Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since her CD4 count (85 cells/uL) independently meets the quantified red-flag threshold that mandates referral.
who_correct_actions: Treat this kind of HIV-linked active case-finding as conditionally appropriate only where the local TB prevalence has been shown to meet the recommended threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), rather than as a routine activity applied irrespective of a demonstrated local prevalence.

Base the decision to refer or escalate her care on individualized clinical judgment of her CD4 count and overall status; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.
us_correct_actions: Attribute her case identification to contact investigation following a known index case rather than population-level active case-finding targeted at a risk group; this framework's primary case-finding model is passive, contact-investigation-driven.

Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding her CD4 count and clinical status, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.
critical_error_conditions: Failing to act on the severely low CD4 count (85 cells/uL) in the context of active TB, leaving the patient on routine outpatient management without any escalation or referral consideration
expected_divergence_points: Whether this patient's HIV-linked active case-finding pathway reflects standard, unconditional national program policy or is only appropriate where a threshold local prevalence is demonstrated
Whether her severely low CD4 count triggers a mandatory, quantified escalation/referral or is left to individualized clinical judgment
